name: UCI Water Treatment Plant
source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, daily monitoring at an urban wastewater treatment plant
citation: Poch, M. (1993). Water Treatment Plant [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5FS4C
data_format: CSV converted from the original UCI comma-separated file
label_note: The data file has no fault labels. The 13 classes in the .names file are the authors' conceptual clusters, not independently confirmed equipment faults, so they are not an anomaly-detection gold standard.
description: Daily records from about 1990–1991 at an urban plant in Spain, covering influent, primary settler, secondary settler, effluent, and the removal figures supplied in the original file.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: Daily influent and effluent BOD, COD, suspended solids, and pH can support a prediction task, but there is no official forecast split and the calendar has gaps.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: The .names file lists 13 conceptual clusters. They are highly imbalanced and are not independent operating-status inspections.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: Suitable for unsupervised screening and for synthetic-anomaly tests reported separately. There is no fault gold standard.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: Plant-wide BOD, COD, suspended solids, and settleable solids have influent, effluent, and the removal figures recorded in the original file.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No micrographs.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: The same day records stage water quality and removal, so process performance can be analyzed directly.

name: IWA BSM1 influent (dry / rain / storm)
source: BSM1 influent files published by the IWA Modelling and Integrated Assessment specialist group
citation: IWA Task Group on Benchmarking of Control Strategies for WWTPs. BSM1 influent files Inf_dry_2006, Inf_rain_2006 and Inf_strm_2006. https://iwa-mia.org/benchmarking/
license: Benchmark influent files posted by the IWA task group. Cite the technical report. This is not an open-source software license.
label_note: The file name is the influent scenario (dry, rain, or storm). Week 1 of the rain and storm files still resembles dry weather, so a file-level label is not an instantaneous weather label. These files contain neither sensor-fault labels nor effluent.
description: Fourteen days of dynamic BSM1 influent, with ASM1 components and flow. Influent dissolved oxygen, nitrate, autotrophs, and particulate products are defined as zero by the benchmark and are not treated as measured dissolved oxygen.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: The 15-minute simulated influent can support load forecasting. It is not measured effluent quality.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: The three influent files are explicit dry, rain, and storm scenarios, but a file-level label is not instantaneous weather and is not an in-plant control state.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: Dry weather can be the reference for deviation screening. The influent files have no fault labels. Faults belong to the separate BSM1_LT benchmark, which is not included.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: Influent only. Removal cannot be computed without effluent.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No images.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: This is the standard influent of a control-strategy benchmark, but simulated effluent and control outputs are not in this repository.

name: DHI Danish WWTP inflow
source: DHI WaterBench: combined-sewer inflow to a Danish WWTP and a nearby weather station
citation: DHI (2025). Inflow to a Waste Water Treatment Plant: observations and processed data [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15301164
label_note: No anomaly or fault labels. Air temperature, pressure, and precipitation come from a weather station, not from the wastewater.
description: About 15 months of WWTP inflow, plus precipitation, pressure, radiation, humidity, and air temperature from the Danish Meteorological Institute. The plant location is anonymized.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: Inflow can be forecast. The file has no pollutant concentrations.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: No operating-condition labels.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: Unsupervised screening only. There are no fault labels.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: No influent or effluent water quality.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No images.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: Inflow and weather drivers can be analyzed. Treatment efficiency cannot.

name: Cologne Weiden WWTP inflow and sewer levels
source: Inflow, sewer levels, and rainfall at the Weiden WWTP in Cologne, Germany
citation: Sonnenschein, B., & Ziel, F. (2022). Wastewater Treatment Plant Inflow Rate, Network Water Levels and Rain Rate for Koeln Weiden, Germany [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6992694
sampling_rate: 15 minutes; interactive detection uses hourly means
label_note: No anomaly labels. Rainfall is a weather driver and is not sent to the detector by default, so rain events are not treated as equipment faults.
description: Inflow, three sewer levels, a storage level, and rain rate for the Cologne Weiden wastewater system. The raw record is 15 minutes.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: Inflow and sewer levels can be forecast. There are no pollutant concentrations.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: No operating-condition labels.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: The multi-sensor series supports unsupervised screening. There are no fault labels.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: No removal rates.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No images.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: Rain, sewer level, and inflow can be compared hydraulically. Biochemical treatment performance cannot.

name: AquaFetch nitrogen and phosphorus recovery experiments
availability: Two experiment tables are bundled. The rest of the AquaFetch collection, about 20,000 experiments, is not packaged here.
source: Zenodo tables used by the AquaFetch wastewater submodule. The underlying experiments are from Leng et al. 2024.
citation: Abbas, A. (2024). Experimental data for P and N recovery from wastewater [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14586314. Experiments: Leng et al., Journal of Water Process Engineering, 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jwpe.2024.104896
sampling_rate: One experiment per row, not a plant time series
label_note: The targets are nitrogen or phosphorus recovery, not plant fault labels.
description: Laboratory adsorption experiments for nitrogen and phosphorus recovery. Useful for treatment-efficiency tasks, not for municipal plant monitoring.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: This is not a plant water-quality time series.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: No operating-status labels.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: Experiment tables are not plant anomaly-detection data.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: Experimental conditions are paired with nitrogen and phosphorus recovery, so treatment efficiency can be predicted. The scope is laboratory recovery.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No images.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: Experiment settings and recovery can be compared. A full-scale plant cannot.

name: MD-AS-2025 activated-sludge microfauna images
availability: Public download. The annotated archive is about 2.0 GB, so this repository stores metadata only.
source: Activated-sludge microfauna images published in Scientific Data. Samples come from a laboratory SBR and 12 plants in six Chinese cities.
citation: Pang, Z. et al. (2025). Image Dataset of Microfauna in Activated Sludge. Scientific Data. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-06228-6
label_note: The annotated set has bounding boxes for testate amoebae, bdelloid rotifers, monogonont rotifers, nematodes, and hypotrichs. There are no segmentation masks.
description: 4,000 boxed full frames and 14,257 single-object crops for microorganism recognition. The images cannot be used to predict COD.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: Images cannot directly predict COD.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: No process operating-status labels.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: No process anomaly labels.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: No removal rates.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: Five microfauna classes and bounding boxes support classification and detection. The images are not packaged in this repository.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: No paired process water-quality table.

name: SWaT water-treatment testbed (A1, Dec 2015)
availability: Request access from iTrust. Redistribution is not allowed, so this repository does not include the files.
source: Secure Water Treatment testbed, iTrust, Singapore University of Technology and Design
citation: iTrust, Centre for Research in Cyber Security, Singapore University of Technology and Design. SWaT dataset. https://www.sutd.edu.sg/itrust/itrust-labs/datasets/dataset-characteristics/swat/
license: iTrust terms: credit the source and do not redistribute
data_format: Historian and network traffic after approval
sampling_rate: A1 is 11 days of continuous operation; the sampling interval is defined in the approved bundle
label_note: A1 has normal and attack labels: 7 normal days, 4 attack days, 51 sensor and actuator channels, and 41 attacks. This is a water-treatment testbed, not a municipal wastewater plant.
description: A water-treatment testbed widely used in industrial-control security research. It is listed to show that a public resource with real attack labels exists, but the files cannot be redistributed.

tasks.name: Water Quality Prediction
tasks.rationale: The testbed is not municipal wastewater monitoring, and this repository is not licensed to use its sensor values.

tasks.name: Operating Condition Classification
tasks.rationale: Normal versus attack can be a state classification, but the states are cyber attacks, not wastewater process conditions.

tasks.name: Anomaly Detection
tasks.rationale: A1 provides normal and attack labels. The data cannot be redistributed, so only task applicability is recorded here.

tasks.name: Treatment Efficiency Prediction
tasks.rationale: No pollutant removal rates.

tasks.name: Microorganism Recognition
tasks.rationale: No micrographs.

tasks.name: Process Performance Analysis
tasks.rationale: This does not represent municipal wastewater treatment performance.
